newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended firm but off highs, although the market proved resilient despite a sharp price drop in the final hour of trade.
The price decline was seen linked to break in the German Bund futures contract below key technical support.

CS Group further increased its new corporate bond launched on Wednesday to 1.0 billion Swiss francs from 750 million francs. The size was already increased shortly after Wednesday's launch from an initial 500 million francs.
Dealers said it was the largest corporate straight ever issued in Swiss francs.
The bond was quoted on dealers' screens late Thursday yielding 3.98 percent at minus 1.50/minus 1.30, up roughly 10 ticks on the price from Wednesday.
The deal met with strong demand, traders said.

"That shows the great demand for Swiss franc paper," said one Swiss-based trader, adding he expected further demand for Swiss bonds as the rest of Europe gears up for the common European "Euro" currency. Uncertainties connected with the Euro should benefit the Swiss bond market, he said.
The Swiss National Bank, as expected, left interest rates unchanged at Thursday's weekly meeting.
Comi medium-term bond COMIc1 up one at 111.05
Euro Swiss francs FESc1 up four at 98.14.
